title: KV prefetch progressive activation with synthetic canary and operator hold
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Add a gated, progressive activation path to automatically apply recommended KV-cache prefetch and batching profiles produced by Optimize. The goal is to realize cost savings without degrading latency or error SLAs by using synthetic canaries, a short rollback runway, and an operator hold step for high-risk deltas. This ticket implements the activation controller, synthetic traffic harness hooks, canary policy config, guardrail thresholds, and an operator approval checkpoint exposed in the Console rollout page.
acceptance_criteria: Controller applies KV prefetch profile to a subset of traffic per policy and records rollout markers in audit logs
Synthetic canary harness injects representative request traces and computes p95/p99 latency, token-throughput, and cache-hit deltas within 30-minute windows
Automatic rollback triggers if latency p95 regresses > 4% or error rate increases > 0.5% over baseline within the canary window
Operator hold created if cost savings > 10% but latency delta between 2% and 4% — requires manual approval to continue
Console shows rollout status, telemetry links, and one-click abort/rollback actions for activations started by Optimize
All changes have an associated GitHub PR, unit tests for controller logic, and an integration test using the synth-canary harness
playbook_steps: 1) Create rollout config: start_fraction=0.5%, step_interval=15m, step_multiplier=2
2) Launch synthetic canary for 30m and collect metrics (p50,p95,p99 latency; errors; cache-hit; tokens/sec)
3) Evaluate against thresholds: abort if p95_regression > 4% OR error_rate_up > 0.5%
4) If cost_savings_estimate > 10% and latency_regression between 2%-4%, create operator hold and notify on-call
5) On operator approval, continue ramping per policy until 50% traffic, then monitor steady-state for 24h before full rollout
6) If any step fails abort and execute automated rollback with revert marker and changelog entry
7) Postmortem: collect canary traces and compare model-level quality metrics; file follow-up if regressions observed
notes: Decision: use synthetic canaries (loadgen+recorded traces) rather than relying solely on live traffic to ensure deterministic baselines for small traffic fractions.
Trade-off: longer synthetic windows increase detection sensitivity but delay cost realization — chose 30m as compromise after SRE review.
Telemetry: kp-metrics dashboards will publish p95 latency, error rate, cache-hit ratio, and estimated per-token cost savings. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/optimize-kv-1001
Guardrails: conservative initial step (0.5%) to minimize blast radius; step_multiplier=2 to ramp quickly on healthy canary while keeping operator visibility.
Rollback hysteresis: require metric recovery for two consecutive canary windows before permitting re-attempt of same profile
Risk: models that are highly sensitive to sequence prefixing may show quality regressions not captured by latency/error metrics — follow-up evals will compare output quality on saved prompt sets.
